answer.evidence: The main body is the ramp, rows 0-31. It is a textured sloped plane seen from above, with chevron and contour marks and no front-edge line or eave shadow. The dark brown, banded strips at its left and right edges are the receding walls of the cut. Rows 32-47 are uniform flat ground (L=136) with no vertical face. The drawing has no south-facing vertical face of 3 or more rows, so it reads as a flat top-down slab. The side walls are visible, but they are not a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's tan peat surface has large areas of one flat colour with no grain, speckle or tuft variation, and the measured near-flat coverage is 33% against 0% for both references. The ramp wedge has only about 4 lightness steps, with a few banded stripes and a dark brown edge. The edges are tinted brown, not black (14% neutral), so the outline is fine. The 10 visible tones per tile is above the grass (3) and close to the paving (7), but the eye reads the tile as broad flat bands. It lacks the per-pixel texture the references carry. It would look flatter next to the references, so it fails.
